newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer-Forex criteria crucial for stable EMU.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer-Forex criteria crucial for stable EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Tuesday that nations must fulfil all entry criteria, including the currency requirement, in order to ensure the currency union will be stable.

"In the interest of a stable currency union all criteria must be fulfilled, this also includes the foreign exchange rate criteria and that a nation needs to be a member of the exchange rate mechanism without a problem," Tietmeyer told a group of bankers.

In a speech prepared for delivery here, Tietmeyer warned, "a nation that cannot keep its exchange rate in the close range of a set rate, obviously has difficulties in keeping its economy in step with those of other currency union candidates."

Tietmeyer, a fervent supporter of a strict interpretation of the entry criteria, added "this is the spirit of the currency criteria and this is true today just as it was when the Maastricht Treaty was signed in 1991."
Stressing that the German constitutional court ruled that the criteria must interpreted strictly, Tietmeyer said that his position does not reflect "narrow minded view" of the Bundesbank.
